question: The 'Bretton Woods Twins' refers to the two multilateral organisations created at the Bretton Woods Conference in 1944. They are ______ and ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**IMF, World Bank**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The 'Bretton Woods Twins' refers to the **International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank**.
 
• Both institutions were established in **1944** during the United Nations Monetary and Financial Conference, commonly known as the Bretton Woods Conference.
 
• The IMF aims to foster global monetary cooperation, secure financial stability, facilitate international trade, promote high employment and sustainable economic growth, and reduce poverty.
 
• The World Bank provides financial and technical assistance to developing countries for development projects (e.g., bridges, roads, schools, etc.) that are expected to improve the economic prospects and quality of life for people in those countries.
 
• The creation of these two institutions marked the beginning of a new era in international economic cooperation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Bretton Woods Conference was held in Bretton Woods, New Hampshire, USA, from July 1 to July 22, 1944.
 
• Delegates from 44 Allied nations attended the conference to regulate the international monetary and financial order after the conclusion of World War II.
 
• The conference led to the establishment of a system of fixed exchange rates and the creation of the Bretton Woods institutions to oversee the international monetary system.
 
• The IMF and World Bank have since played a crucial role in the global economy, providing financial assistance and policy advice to countries around the world.
